text:
Two particles A and B having charges 20$μ$C and $-$5$μ$C respectively are held fixed with a separation of 5 cm. At what position a third charged particle should be placed so that it does not experience a net electric force?


[IMG]
options: At 5 cm from 20 $μ$C on the left side of system
At 5 cm from $-$5 $μ$C on the right side
At 1.25 cm from $-$5 $μ$C between two charges
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A third charge $q$ feels no net force where the net electric field of A and B is zero, since $F=qE$.

Between the charges the fields of $+20μ\text{C}$ and $-5μ\text{C}$ both point towards B, so they cannot cancel there. For unlike charges the null point lies outside, nearer the smaller charge, i.e. to the right of B.


[IMG]

For a point N at distance $x$ (in cm) to the right of B:

$\dfrac{k(20μ\text{C})}{(5+x)^{2}}=\dfrac{k(5μ\text{C})}{x^{2}}\Rightarrow (5+x)^{2}=4x^{2}$

$5+x=2x\Rightarrow x=5\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift

text: A body of mass M moving at speed $V_{0}$ collides elastically with a mass 'm' at rest. After the collision, the two masses move at angles $θ_{1}$ and $θ_{2}$ with respect to the initial direction of motion of the body of mass M. The largest possible value of the ratio M/m, for which the angles $θ_{1}$ and $θ_{2}$ will be equal, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Given $θ_{1}$ = $θ_{2}$ = $θ$

from momentum conservation

in x-direction $MV_{0} = MV_{1} \cos θ$ $+ mV_{2} \cos θ$

in y-direction $0 = MV_{1} \sin θ$ $-$ $mV_{2} \sin θ$

Solving above equations

$V_{2}=\frac{MV_{1}}{m}$, $V_{0} = 2V_{1} \cos θ$

From energy conservation

$\frac{1}{2}MV_{0}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}MV_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}mV_{2}^{2}$

Substituting value of $V_{2}$ & $V_{0}$, we will get

$\frac{M}{m}+1=4\cos ^{2}θ\leq 4$

$\frac{M}{m}\leq 3$

Option (c)

text: For an ideal gas the instantaneous change in pressure 'p' with volume 'v' is given by the equation $\frac{dp}{dv}=-ap$. If $p = p_{0}$ at  v =0 is the given boundary condition, then the maximum temperature one mole of gas can attain is : (Here R is the gas constant)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{p_{0}}^{p}\frac{dp}{P}=-a\int\limits _{0}^{v}dv$

$\ln \left (\frac{p}{p_{0}}\right )=-av$

$p=p_{0}e^{-av}$

For temperature maximum p-v product should be maximum

$T=\frac{pv}{nR}=\frac{p_{0}ve^{-av}}{R}$

$\frac{dT}{dv}=0\Rightarrow \frac{p_{0}}{R}\{e^{-av}+ve^{-av}(-a)\}$ = 0

$\frac{p_{0}e^{-av}}{R}\{1-av\}=0$

$v=\frac{1}{a},\infty$

$T=\frac{p_{0}1}{Rae}=\frac{p_{0}}{Rae}$

at v = $\infty$

T = 0

Option (a)

text:
Which of the following equations is dimensionally incorrect?

Where t = time, h = height, s = surface tension, $θ$ = angle, $ρ$ = density, a, r = radius, g = acceleration due to gravity, v = volume, p = pressure, W = work done, $\Gamma$ = torque, $\in$ = permittivity, E = electric field, J = current density, L = length.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Poiseuille's equation gives the volume of liquid flowing per unit time, $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=\dfrac{πpa^{4}}{8ηL}$, where $η$ is the coefficient of viscosity.

(A) $\left [\dfrac{πpa^{4}}{8ηL}\right ]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{M}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{T}^{-2}][\mathrm{L}^{4}]}{[\mathrm{M}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{T}^{-1}][\mathrm{L}]}=[\mathrm{L}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-1}]$, while a volume has $[\mathrm{L}^{3}]$, so this equation is dimensionally incorrect.

(B) Capillary rise: $\left [\dfrac{2s\cos θ}{ρrg}\right ]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{M}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]}{[\mathrm{M}\mathrm{L}^{-3}][\mathrm{L}][\mathrm{L}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]}=[\mathrm{L}]=[h]$.

(C) By Gauss's law $\in E$ equals a charge per unit area, so $\left [\in \dfrac{𝜕E}{𝜕t}\right ]=\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}\mathrm{T}]}{[\mathrm{L}^{2}][\mathrm{T}]}=[\mathrm{A}\mathrm{L}^{-2}]=[J]$; this is the displacement current density.

(D) $θ$ is dimensionless, so $[\Gamma θ]=[\mathrm{M}\mathrm{L}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}]=[W]$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift

text: A car is moving on a plane inclined at 30${}^{\circ }$ to the horizontal with an acceleration of $10 ms^{-2}$ parallel to the plane upward. A bob is suspended by a string from the roof of the car. The angle in degrees which the string makes with the vertical is $______________. ($Take $g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

Angle of inclination, $θ$ = 30${}^{\circ }$

Acceleration, $a = 10 ms^{-2}$

Acceleration due to gravity, $g = 10 ms^{-2}$

According to the question the car and bob is as shown below,


[IMG]


Here, F' is the pseudo force acting on the bob when we considered it from car's frame and T is the tension on the string.

In equilibrium, $\SigmaF_{x} = 0$ and $\SigmaF_{y} = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ F' cos30${}^{\circ }$ = T sin$α$

$\frac{ma\cos 30^{\circ }}{\sin α}=T$ ...... (i)

where, m is the mass of the bob.

$F^{'}\sin 30^{\circ }+mg=T\cos α$

$\Rightarrow ma\sin 30^{\circ }+mg=\frac{ma\cos 30^{\circ }}{\sin α}(\cos α)$ [$\because$ using Eq. (i)]

$\Rightarrow a\sin 30^{\circ }+g=\frac{a\cos 30^{\circ }}{\sin α}(\cos α)$

$10\times \frac{1}{2}+10=\frac{10\times \sqrt{3}}{2}\cot α$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cot α\Rightarrow \frac{3}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cot α$

or, $\cot α=\sqrt{3}$

$\Rightarrow α=30^{\circ }$
